requirements.title: Omitted SIGN= defaults to PROCESSOR_DEFINED and leaves the behavior processor defined
requirements.definition: If SIGN= is omitted in an OPEN statement that initiates a formatted connection, the default value is PROCESSOR_DEFINED; the particular sign behavior selected by that processor-defined mode is not fixed by this unit.

pending.sign-default-token-processor-defined: Concrete INQUIRE plan: OPEN a named file with FORM='FORMATTED' while omitting SIGN=, prefill a default-character SIGN inquiry variable with a nonmatching sentinel such as '#################', then INQUIRE by unit with SIGN=. Per 12.10.2.30, SIGN= is assigned PLUS, SUPPRESS, or PROCESSOR_DEFINED corresponding to the sign mode in effect for a formatted connection; 12.5.6.18 makes the omitted OPEN default PROCESSOR_DEFINED, so assert exactly the token PROCESSOR_DEFINED (with only blank padding if the variable is longer).
pending.sign-default-behavior-processor-dependen: No portable oracle exists for the particular sign behavior selected by PROCESSOR_DEFINED; future fixtures must pin SIGN=PLUS or SUPPRESS when they need exact optional-plus behavior.

review_rationale: Source registration for the OPEN statement and its specifiers, 12.5.6.1-12.5.6.19 (batch151). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across four rounds. Round 1 found required OPEN defaults with only generic plans and required default tokens over-suppressed as unobservable; both are now concrete sentinel-prefilled INQUIRE plans (ACCESS, ASYNCHRONOUS, BLANK, DECIMAL, DELIM, FORM, PAD, LEADING_ZERO, SIGN, and ROUND as set membership). Rounds 2 and 3 found that INQUIRE(POSITION=) reports connection STATE, not the omitted OPEN token, and that a re-OPEN plan observes 12.5.6.1 p6 rather than the POSITION default; the omitted POSITION= token is now recorded as not portably observable, as are the STATUS and ENCODING default tokens. The eight numbered rules R1204-R1207 and C1203-C1206 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
